metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Limited at practice Thursday

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Upgrades to Limited Practice on Thursday
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in practice on Thursday. It is a notable development after he did not practice at all with the team on Wednesday. Meyers has been a regular on the team's practice report this year, but he has not missed any games, and his return to practice on Thursday should mean that he will be fine to play this weekend in a divisional tilt on Sunday on the road against the Tennessee Titans. The 30-year-old veteran has been a regular contributor in his first full season with the Jags in 2026 as the WR2 behind Parker Washington, catching 26 passes for 374 yards and two touchdowns in his eight games played. However, Meyers has not found the end zone since Week 3 against the New England Patriots, and he is still searching for his first 100-yard game of the year. Fantasy managers will want to check back on his final status on Friday, but if Meyers ends up playing against the Titans this weekend, he will be a solid WR3/flex with a good chance to find the end zone for the third time this year. He caught four of his six targets for 65 yards in last Thursday night's rout over the Baltimore Ravens.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) misses practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers did not practice on Wednesday.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Remains a Reliable Target for Jaguars
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle) remains involved in the passing game each week. He ranks second on the team in receiving yards (354), tied for second in targets (37), third in receptions (26), and tied for third in touchdown receptions (two) in 2026. Meyers is behind only fellow wide receiver Parker Washington in yards and targets, and is behind Washington and tight end Brenton Strange in receptions. Most recently, Meyers earned six targets in a 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 9, and recorded four receptions for 65 yards (16.3 yards per catch). Meyers and the Jaguars get a Week 10 matchup with a Tennessee Titans defense that allows 258.3 passing yards per game, which ranks second-to-last in the NFL. The Titans also allow 24.9 points per game (22nd in the NFL). Meyers ranks as RotoBaller's No. 30 wide receiver for Week 10, and he has a favorable matchup against the Titans.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Doesn't practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Meyers (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
metadata.analysis: Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week, before playing 68 percent of snaps and catching four passes for 65 yards in a Thursday blowout at Baltimore. It's unclear if he ankle has worsened or Wednesday's absence is just a matter of caution/maintenance. Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would all be candidates for additional WR snaps if Meyers were to miss time this year.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers snags four passes in win
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers caught four of six passes for 65 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Meyers led the team in receptions and yards, while coming in second in targets. It was the veteran's second-best yardage total of the season, and he now has 65 yards or more in two of his last three games.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Paces pass catchers in win
metadata.description: Meyers brought in four of six targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
metadata.analysis: Meyers set the pace for the Jaguars in both receptions and receiving yards on the night, bouncing back nicely from a quiet 2-24-0 line just four days earlier in a blowout win over the Colts. The veteran wideout has multiple catches in all but one game, although Meyers hasn't topped 83 receiving yards in any contest to date in 2026. Meyers remains a key target for Trevor Lawrence, but he could see at least a slight boost in his outlook heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15, if Brian Thomas is moved at the trade deadline.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers a Low-Upside Flex in Week 9
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers remains a borderline flex option in Week 9 against the Baltimore Ravens after limited practice participation all week. The Ravens defense ranks 25th against wide receivers in fantasy, but Meyers has only popped in one game all season, which happened to be against his former team, the New England Patriots, in Week 3. Meyers has never been a big red-zone threat in his career, so beyond PPR leagues, the veteran receiver has never had the greatest upside. Game script has also been a limiting factor this season. Despite the team winning 42-7 against the Indianapolis Colts last week, Meyers finished with just two catches for 24 yards on just three targets due to the Jacksonville rushing attack and defense dominating. Unless the Ravens without Lamar Jackson somehow make it a close game, it is hard to imagine Meyers's volume being that different. His consistent but relatively minimal involvement in the potent Jacksonville offense makes Meyers a barely startable option in Week 9.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) off injury report for Thursday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is off of the injury report for Thursday night's game against the Baltimore Ravens.
metadata.analysis: Meyers has been dealing with a pair of injuries lately, but neither of them are serious and he will be good to go for Thursday night's game. He isn't expected to be a reliable fantasy option on a week-to-week basis even if active, however.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Good to go for TNF
metadata.description: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) does not carry an injury designation going into Thursday's game at the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: Though Meyers was limited in practice, the Jaguars are not listing him on the injury report going into Thursday's game. The veteran has battled through bumps and bruises throughout the season but has yet to miss a game. He'll be good to go for Week 9 in Charm City.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Has No Injury Designation for Thursday
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) carries no injury designation for Thursday night's Week 9 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens despite being limited in practice throughout the week. Meyers played through both injuries during Sunday's 42-7 victory over Indianapolis, catching two of three targets for 24 yards. Jacksonville attempted just 17 passes in that contest, limiting receiving opportunities across the offense. The 29-year-old has caught 22 passes for 309 yards and two touchdowns through seven appearances, with his best recent performance coming against Houston in Week 6, when he recorded five receptions for 83 yards on 10 targets. His expected availability is encouraging, but inconsistent target volume remains the bigger concern for fantasy managers. Meyers is best viewed as a matchup-dependent flex option rather than a reliable weekly starter.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Remains limited in Tuesday's practice
metadata.description: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) limited in practice Tuesday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers was limited in practice on Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: Meyers is on track to be good to go. He'll remain a fringe WR3/WR4 for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Limited Again on Tuesday
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring, ankle) was listed as a limited participant in practice on Tuesday for the second straight day. Meyers is battling through multiple injuries and also put in two limited practices last week before sitting out of Friday's practice. The 29-year-old still ended up suiting up in the Week 8 blowout win over the Indianapolis Colts, but he caught just two of his three targets for a season-low 24 yards. Meyers' muted production on Sunday most likely had more to do with the blowout nature of the game against the Colts than anything else, and he should be ready to go on a short turnaround to kick off Week 9 action this Thursday night in a good matchup against the banged-up Baltimore Ravens. In his first full season in Jacksonville, Meyers has caught 22 of his 31 targets for 309 yards (14.0 yards per reception) and two touchdowns. Both he and Brian Thomas Jr. have taken a back seat to Parker Washington, but as long as he is active for Thursday Night Football, Meyers should be treated as a WR4/flex option for fantasy managers this week.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Has hamstring, ankle injuries
metadata.description: Meyers was listed as limited on Monday's estimated injury report due to hamstring and ankle issues.
metadata.analysis: Meyers was capped at Monday's walkthrough as a result of the health concerns that impacted him in practice last week, but he still suited up Sunday versus the Colts, handling a 54 percent snap share and gathering in two of three targets for 24 yards. Considering he was able to play through them in Week 8, he's likely trending toward being available Thursday in Baltimore, but his status nonetheless will be watched to ensure as much.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Quiet performance on run-heavy day
metadata.description: Meyers logged two catches for 24 yards on three targets in Sunday's 42-7 win against Indianapolis.
metadata.analysis: He put up a subpar fantasy line, but Meyers actually led Jacksonville in targets and tied for the team lead in receptions on a day when quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw only 14 passes, 10 of which he completed. Meyers also logged a 54 percent offensive snap share -- second among Jaguars wideouts behind Parker Washington -- after dealing with a hamstring injury during the week. He's still looking to build some momentum, as Meyers has three or fewer catches in five of his seven contests and has topped 40 receiving yards just twice.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers is Limited on Monday's Injury Report
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring, ankle) was listed as a limited participant during Monday's walkthrough. metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers finishes with a pair of receptions in Week 8

Assuming he's deemed active approximately 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, he'll be looking to build upon the season-high 83 receiving yards he put up in the Jaguars' last game in Week 6 against the Texans in London.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers active Sunday vs. Colts
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) is officially active for Sunday's divisional matchup against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8, according to John Shipley of Sports Illustrated. Meyers was questionable to play this weekend after missing Friday's practice, but the 29-year-old will suit up for a good matchup. It is bad news as Brian Thomas Jr. looks to get more involved to make himself more attractive before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Meyers comes out of Jacksonville's Week 7 bye with 20 catches on 28 targets for 285 yards and two touchdowns in his first six games of his first full season with the Jaguars. Meyers is coming off a strong game in the team's last contest in London against the division-rival Houston Texans in Week 6, when he caught five of a season-high 10 targets for a season-high 83 yards, but he has not found the end zone since a Week 3 win over the New England Patriots. The former undrafted free agent from NC State found the end zone twice in the first two weeks of the 2026 campaign and will try to find paydirt for the third time against the floundering Colts. RotoBaller has Meyers ranked as a WR3/flex option in Week 8.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Suiting Up for Week 8 Against the Colts
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring, ankle) is "good to go" for Sunday's Week 8 contest against the Indianapolis Colts, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL.com. Meyers had been listed as questionable after missing Friday's practice, but ultimately, the injury won't sideline him for this week's divisional battle. Prior to the Jaguars' Week 7 bye, Meyers had a solid showing in London with 10 targets, five catches, and a season-high 83 receiving yards against the Houston Texans. He has carved out a sizable role with Brian Thomas Jr. seemingly in the doghouse, as Meyers is now the clear-cut No. 2 receiver behind Parker Washington in Jacksonville. He should continue to rank as a solid WR3 option in fantasy football ahead of Sunday's matchup against a Colts team that has already started to trade away players on both sides of the ball.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers a Reasonable Flex Despite Injury Concerns
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) missed Friday's practice, making his status truly questionable. If he does play, the veteran receiver feels like a solid fantasy option in a Week 8 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts. The Colts seem to be at their most vulnerable after beginning to trade top veterans and losing to the now one-win Tennessee Titans in Week 6. Meyers is clearly behind Parker Washington in the receiver pecking order, but he does feel like the clear WR2 in the offense with Brian Thomas Jr. losing playing time. In Week 6, Meyers finished with five catches for 83 yards, his best receiving output of the season. It will be worth monitoring his injury status as the first slate of Sunday games approaches, but the vet still feels like a solid fantasy option. Meyers should continue to earn volume, unless the Jaguars decide to limit him to keep him healthy in what could be a blowout victory. For now, Meyers is a solid Flex option for fantasy managers in Week 8.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Questionable After Missing Friday's Practice
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring, ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts after missing Friday's practice. Meyers was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out the final session, raising concerns about his availability following Jacksonville's Week 7 bye. The 29-year-old has played all six games this season, catching 20 of 28 targets for 285 yards and two touchdowns. He was heavily involved against Houston in Week 6, recording five receptions for 83 yards on a season-high 10 targets. Parker Washington led Jacksonville with 11 targets in that contest, while Brenton Strange drew seven, making both potential beneficiaries if Meyers cannot play. The veteran's inconsistent target volume already made him a matchup-dependent flex option, and Friday's missed practice adds another concern for fantasy managers considering him against Indianapolis.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Remains a Usable Floor-Play Coming off a Season-Best Performance
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers is coming off his most involved game of the season and should continue to provide a usable fantasy floor moving forward. Before a Week 7 bye, Meyers saw 10 targets in a narrow loss to the Texans, his highest total since the mid-season trade that landed him in Jacksonville in 2025, while his 83 receiving yards were his second-most as a Jaguar. Fourth-year player Parker Washington has emerged as the star of Jacksonville's passing offense, but Meyers remains one of the most consistent complementary pieces in the NFL, and he is RotoBaller's WR40 ahead of a Week 8 divisional matchup with the Colts.

Unless the hamstring injury was something that cropped up during Wednesday's practice, Meyers' ability to begin Week 8 prep on the field in some capacity is generally a good sign for his chances of suiting up Sunday versus the Colts.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers' 10-Target Game Boosts Week 8 Waiver Appeal
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers makes a compelling case for a Week 8 waiver claim in 10-team and deeper PPR leagues after drawing more targets against the Houston Texans in Week 6 than in his previous two games combined. Meyers caught five of 10 targets for a season-high 83 yards in the 34-31 loss after totaling five catches for 70 yards on seven targets in Weeks 4 and 5. His expanded involvement offers flex potential following Jacksonville's bye, although he has been held to 40 receiving yards or fewer in four of six appearances. Meyers has 20 catches for 285 yards and two touchdowns on 28 targets overall. He faces considerable competition for Trevor Lawrence's attention, with Parker Washington drawing 11 targets against Houston and Brenton Strange receiving seven. The Jaguars host the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers hauls in five passes in Week 6 loss
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers caught 5-of-10 targets for 83 yards in a 34-31 loss to Houston.
metadata.analysis: Meyers lead the team in catches and receiving Sunday, falling just one target behind Parker Washington for the team lead. The veteran turned in his best performance of the season so far and will look to build on that after their bye week in Week 7.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Leading receiver in Week 6 loss
metadata.description: Meyers caught five of 10 targets for 83 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
metadata.analysis: While Parker Washington led the Jaguars with 11 looks from Trevor Lawrence, Meyers paced the club in catches and receiving yards on his largest target volume of the season. The 83 yards were also a season best for Meyers, and the veteran wideout will take a 20-285-2 line on 28 targets into a bye before clashing with the Colts in Week 8.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers a Strong Streamer in Favorable Spot
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers is a fine option off the waiver wire for Week 6's matchup with their division-rival Houston Texans in London. Meyers joined Jacksonville in a trade with the Raiders at last season's deadline and became a go-to target during the team's playoff push. In 2026, the veteran's role has taken a step back, acting as little more than a tertiary option in the Jags' attack. That said, Meyers currently ranks third among Jacksonville's pass catchers in receptions (15), yards (202), and targets (18). While it may not always show up in the box score due to a run-heavy game plan, the 29-year-old has been involved. He's worth streaming consideration, especially against a Texans defense that hasn't been as formidable as it was in 2025.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers an Under-the-Radar Waiver-Wire Target
metadata.description: Across five games so far in 2026, Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers has recorded 15 catches for 202 yards and two touchdowns on 18 targets. While the veteran wideout's numbers don't jump off the page, his limited production is partially a function of his team's run-heavy game scripts. Through five weeks, Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence is averaging just 28.6 pass attempts per game. Meyers leads Jacksonville wide receivers in snaps, and he's established himself as the team's clear WR2 alongside breakout wideout Parker Washington. If the Jaguars are forced to turn to the air a bit more going forward, Meyers could be well-positioned for an uptick in his numbers. In leagues where he remains available, Meyers could be an under-the-radar waiver wire target for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Limited production in Week 5
metadata.description: Meyers caught two of three targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 19-17 win against the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: Meyers was limited to 40 or fewer receiving yards for the fourth time this season, and he finished tied with running back Bhayshul Tuten for fourth on the team in targets Sunday. Meyers has solidified himself as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind Parker Washington early in the season, but his production hasn't been that notable. Through five games, Meyers has caught 15 of 18 targets for 202 yards and two touchdowns.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers finishes with two grabs in Sunday's win
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers caught 2-of-3 targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: Meyers continues to be a reliable receiver for QB Trevor Lawrence, but he has now finished with three or fewer grabs and no more than 40 yards in four of the first five games of the season. Meyers seems to be the third option in the passing game behind top wideout Parker Washington and TE Brenton Strange. Rookie Josh Cameron is on the ascent too.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Offers Upside as Jaguars Head to London
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers has been the team's second WR this season and is in a pair of favorable matchups the next two weeks. He has actually played more snaps than any other WR for the Jags, although Parker Washington is getting more targets. Meyers has two touchdowns in his four games this season and has 10 catches for 97 yards in the last two weeks in wins over the Patriots and Bengals. He can be a deep-league FLEX option in the next two weeks as the Jaguars face the Eagles and the Texans in their two games in London. Both the Eagles and Texans rank in the top 10 in most fantasy points allowed to receivers this season, and Meyers is involved enough to bring upside from the waiver wire if you need short-term help at the position due to bye weeks or injuries.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers catches three passes Sunday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers caught three passes for 33 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wasn't able to do much of note on Sunday, finishing with just 33 yards in a narrow win over the Bengals. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be relevant moving forward, however, especially with some tough matchups coming up for Jacksonville's offense over the next two weeks.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Three catches in win
metadata.description: Meyers caught three of four targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 22-17 win against the Bengals.
metadata.analysis: Meyers finished second on the team in targets behind tight end Brenton Strange (eight), but his performance was far from noteworthy. The wide receiver has operated as a distant No. 2 option behind Parker Washington at his position this season, and Sunday's performance was his third game with 40 or fewer receiving yards over four contests.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Looking to Build Off Last Week's Big Game
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers is trending up in fantasy football. After catching just three passes through the first two weeks, Meyers exploded with seven catches, 64 yards, and one touchdown last Sunday against his old team, the New England Patriots. Parker Washington is still the top Jaguars receiver in fantasy football, but Meyers' big performance in Week 3 has cemented him as a strong WR3/flex option going forward. Meyers ranks first in the NFL in target separation against man coverage this year, and he also ranks first in quarterback rating when targeted. The underlying metrics suggest that Meyers should have a much bigger role than he has occupied this season, so we don't think that his big Week 3 was any sort of fluke. This week, he'll also benefit from a matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, whose pass defense has been nothing special. Cincinnati ranks near the middle of the league with the 15th-fewest fantasy points allowed to wide receivers in 2026.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Good to go for Week 4

Meyers was targeted a season-high eight times last Sunday against the Patriots but has just 11 targets on the season over three games. He's a low-floor WR4 for fantasy, but this game does have some shootout appeal.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Limited with thumb issue

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers leads team in receiving Sunday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers caught 7-of-8 targets for 64 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Meyers had a fantastic game against his former team on Sunday. He led the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards over the course of the afternoon and was also able to score a touchdown, which was the cherry on top. This was a good game for the veteran, but fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to put up numbers like this week-in and week-out moving forward.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers a Top Waiver Priority After His Best Game of the Season
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers caught a season-high seven passes for 64 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's blowout win over his former team, the Patriots. After a quiet start to the season in which he was targeted only three times in the first two weeks, Meyers appears to have emerged as the team's second receiver, coming up big in a game in which the defensive game plan limited Parker Washington to a season-low three catches. What was seen as one of the most wide-open receiver rooms coming into the season looks to have developed a clear hierarchy, with both Meyers and Washington holding a near-every-down role. Meanwhile, Brian Thomas Jr. has found himself in a rotation with sixth-round rookie Josh Cameron, and two-way player Travis Hunter continues to feature primarily on defense, seeing only five offensive snaps in Week 3. Meyers remains a flex-worthy play moving forward and should be viewed as a priority waiver add wherever available.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Finds paydirt in blowout win
metadata.description: Meyers caught seven of eight targets for 64 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 35-6 win over New England.
metadata.analysis: Meyers led the team in targets, most notably reeling in a 10-yard score from quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the second quarter. The touchdown was the second of the year for the wide receiver, and he has now caught 10 of 11 targets for 132 yards over three contests in 2026. Parker Washington has established himself as Lawrence's favorite target, but Meyers has found himself on equal footing with fellow wideout Brian Thomas as an unpredictable fantasy asset early in the season.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers a Deep-League Flex Against Patriots
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (thumb) practiced fully on Friday and is good to go for a Week 3 matchup with the New England Patriots. Meyers has been busy in terms of playing time to start the year but has been out-produced by both Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. He did manage to score in Week 1, but he has only had three catches through two games. The veteran receiver played 90% of the snaps in Week 2, which is promising, but playing time doesn't matter if you aren't earning targets. There is the narrative of Meyers facing one of his former teams, but that isn't enough of a boost for him to be viewed as a reliable fantasy starter. Meyers has a chance to produce more given his performance at the end of last season, but for now he shouldn't be trusted beyond deeper leagues in Week 3.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is good to go for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
metadata.analysis: As expected, the veteran wideout's thumb injury is not a serious issue for him and he will play through it on Sunday. He will be up against his former team on Sunday, but fantasy managers still shouldn't consider him a trustworthy option in that interesting matchup.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Avoids injury designation
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Meyers quietly leads the Jaguars with an 86 percent route share, but he's been targeted on just 6 percent of his routes, taking a backseat to Parker Washington and Brian Thomas, in that order. Thomas' sloppy play in a Week 2 loss at Denver could perhaps push more volume in Meyers' direction, though that's likely to happen in any case even if his thumb injury continues to linger.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Barely Seeing the Ball in Jacksonville
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers has been on the field plenty, but the targets have almost vanished. Meyers caught both of his looks for 40 yards and a touchdown in Week 1, then saw only one target against Denver and turned it into a 28-yard catch. He still played 54 snaps and ran a team-high 29 routes in that loss. Trevor Lawrence just kept going elsewhere, with Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. combining for 20 targets. That is a rough change for Meyers after he averaged nearly seven targets per game in nine appearances with Jacksonville last season, catching 42 passes for 483 yards and three touchdowns. The thumb injury is still being managed, but Meyers has not missed a game because of it. RotoBaller has him at WR54 for Week 3 against New England. The routes are keeping him on the fantasy radar for now, but three targets in two games is nowhere near enough to trust in a lineup.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Remains limited Thursday
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The Jaguars put a cap on Meyers' reps for the second day in a row, but head coach Liam Coen hasn't provided any indication that the wideout is at any real risk of sitting out Sunday's game against the Patriots while he continues to manage a right thumb injury that dates back to training camp. Meyers played through the thumb issue in the first two contests of the season, recording three catches for 68 yards and a touchdown on three targets.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) listed as limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran should be fine to play in Week 3, despite being limited at practice all week so far. Barring any setbacks with his recovery, he should be a full go against his former team on Sunday but still doesn't project to be a strong option from a fantasy perspective.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Limited in Wednesday's practice
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant for Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
metadata.analysis: The veteran has been held back in practice for much of the season due to a thumb issue, but it hasn't prevented him from suiting up on Sundays. Look for the Jaguars to continue to manage Meyers' injury cautiously in practices to keep him fresh on gamedays. The wideout still looks to be on track to play Week 3 versus the Patriots.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) a limited participant Wednesday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: A thumb injury left Meyers limited at Jacksonville's first practice of the week on Wednesday. It doesn't seem likely to affect his availability for Week 3, however, and he should continue to play his usual role in a matchup against his former team, the Patriots, this week if he suffers no setbacks in his recovery.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers held to one catch in Week 2
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers caught his lone target for a 28-yard gain in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Meyers didn't record his lone catch of the game until the fourth quarter as he took a backseat to both Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. Meyers has now caught all three of his targets for 68 yards and a touchdown through two games this season. He will be a flex consideration heading into Week 3 against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Draws one target in Week 2
metadata.description: Meyers secured his only target for 28 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
metadata.analysis: On a day Trevor Lawrence threw for just 189 yards on 29 attempts, Parker Washington and Brian Thomas combined to see 20 of those targets. Meyers dealt with a thumb injury during the practice week but still led all wideouts with 54 snaps against Denver, running a team-high 29 routes. Through two games, Meyers has just three catches for 68 yards and a touchdown on three targets. He's tough to get behind as anything more than a fantasy WR4 ahead of next Sunday's game against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Meyers was on the injury report all week due to a lingering wrist issue, but he is going to be good to go and will play in Sunday's game against the Broncos. Fantasy managers shouldn't trust in his week-to-week consistency at this point in the season, however, especially in what projects to be a tough matchup.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers a Solid PPR Flex Option in Week 2
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited at practice all week but is good to go against the Denver Broncos in Week 2. The Jaguars' passing attack will look to continue its stellar play stemming from last season against a defense with a strong reputation. However, the Kansas City Chiefs gashed the Broncos last week in a 31-10 victory, and the Jaguars scored 34 points on the Broncos in Denver just last season. Those signs point to what could be another great offensive outing, even in a much harder matchup than the Cleveland Browns from Week 1. Meyers doesn't have the upside of a Brian Thomas Jr. or Parker Washington, but he does have a decent floor, especially in PPR leagues. It is also promising that Meyers led Jaguars receivers in Week 1 snaps, although Thomas Jr. did miss some time in the first half with a shoulder injury. The Jaguars have a crowded room of pass catchers, but the offense does spread the ball around, meaning Meyers should be viewed as a flex option with a limited ceiling against the Broncos.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Ready for Week 2
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) was limited at Friday's practice but doesn't have an injury designation for Week 2 at Denver, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
metadata.analysis: Brian Thomas (shoulder) also avoided an injury designation despite being limited in practice throughout the week. He picked up his injury during the Week 1 win over Cleveland, whereas Meyers is listed with the same thumb injury that he played through successfully in the season opener.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers Will Play in Week 2 in Denver
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited in practice all week, but he does not carry an injury designation on Friday's final injury report and will play in Week 2 on Sunday in Denver against the Broncos, per The Florida Times-Union's Ryan O'Halloran. Meyers, who was a bit of a forgotten man during the summer in training camp, caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the season-opening win over the Cleveland Browns. The 29-year-old dealt with a thumb injury late in training camp, but it was nothing serious, and he was able to play in the season opener. Now that he is officially cleared for Week 2, Meyers should be considered a WR3/4 in his second game of the 2026 season as he competes for targets with Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. In last year's 34-20 win over the Broncos in Denver in Week 16, Meyers caught four of his eight targets for 45 yards.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) limited participant Thursday
metadata.description: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran was again a limited participant on Thursday, which was to be expected, as the team has left him limited at all of their official practices so far in the regular season. He should be good to go for Week 2 and will see more work than usual if Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) is sidelined against the Broncos.

metadata.title: Jakobi Meyers - Remains limited in practice
metadata.description: Meyers (thumb) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Meyers emerged from preseason Week 2 with a brace on his right hand, but the nature of the injury wasn't confirmed until the Jaguars posted their first injury report of the season last week. Since then, he's been listed as limited on all five of the team's practice reports with a thumb injury, but it didn't stop him from suiting up for this past Sunday's season-opening win against the Browns, when he hauled in both targets for 40 yards and one touchdown and recorded one carry for two yards on a 65 percent snap share. If Meyers follows last week's trajectory this week, he'll enter the weekend without a designation for Sunday's contest at Denver.
